quarterly_data.figure: hardware approximately 10% of total company revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nikesh Arora, largest Q4 wins (unnamed customers): a $126 million agreement with a global telecoms leader standardizing on its network security platforms (Next-Generation Firewall plus Prisma Access SASE displacing legacy proxy providers); a $72 million transaction with a premier IT service provider with eight-figure investments in each of Network & AI Security, Cortex and Idira; a $53 million platformization deal with a leading global payments platform that committed high seven figures to Prisma AIRS.

CEO Nikesh Arora: XSIAM ended the year with over $700 million in ARR, up 70%, and passed 1,000 customers; observability ARR more than doubled since the Chronosphere acquisition closed in Q2 to above $500 million (bought at $85 million ARR), and XSIAM plus observability exceed $1 billion in ARR; XSIAM contributed to 50% of net new Chronosphere logos; Q4 included a $20 million deal with a hypergrowth AI inference provider processing tens of trillions of tokens a day, and Q4 net new ARR included a nine-figure benefit from a large LLM customer migrating to Chronosphere from an incumbent vendor (CFO); a majority of Chronosphere's customers are AI-native, including a very large frontier AI lab; the CEO says Chronosphere is on average 30% or 40% cheaper than leading incumbents, is sold only to AI natives for now, and he expects it to be enterprise-competitive within the next six months with Embrace (acquired) and Synthetics.
quarterly_data.figure: XSIAM ARR above $700 million, up 70%; observability ARR above $500 million; $20 million AI inference provider deal

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nikesh Arora: a new vanguard of buyers - sovereigns, neoclouds and frontier labs deploying massive computational capacity that must be secured - produced multiple seven-figure bookings in Q4; firewall execution drove accelerated FY2026 bookings on demand for 5th-generation hardware and software firewalls; agentic traffic on the SASE platform surged 9x over the last nine months; Palo Alto Networks blocks more than 30 billion attacks in a single day. quarterly_data.figure: 400+ shared leads; 200+ net new logos; $5 million+ TCV deals up 50%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nikesh Arora: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have come to the table in partnerships, giving early access to their models; Palo Alto Networks is the first commercial partner allowed to use Mythos in its testing harness (first certified commercial partner for Mythos 5) and already uses OpenAI 5.6 in that harness; it can build and deploy signatures for OT and open-source vulnerabilities in under four hours versus a 55-day patching standard; the Frontier AI Critical Defense Program was expanded last month with a multi-modal harness.

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nikesh Arora: the global AI infrastructure build-out is drawing trillions in investment - 'We anticipate more capital expenditure in the next five years than the preceding two decades', fueled by demand that continues to outstrip supply; 'if you believe that we're going to spend $5 trillion of CapEx in the next five years building data centers and AI capability', AI must add tremendous enterprise value; there is approximately $1 trillion of global cybersecurity debt to modernize; he suspects there will be some major breaches over the coming years and calls AI a long-term tailwind for the sector.
